title: Deepfake regulation - is India drafting a dedicated law
p1: A video of a public figure says something shocking. Millions watch it. But what if the person never said those words? The biggest challenge of deepfakes is not creating fake content — it is making people doubt what is real.
p2: Many believe India already has a complete deepfake law. The reality is different. Existing rules under IT laws and criminal provisions can address some misuse, but there is still debate around whether India needs a dedicated framework specifically for AI-generated fake videos, audio, and images.
p3: A dedicated law would not only focus on punishment. It may also need clear rules for detection, platform responsibility, consent, and protection against identity misuse. One surprising point: even genuine videos can become less trustworthy when people know deepfakes are easy to create. The practical lesson is simple — digital evidence may need stronger verification before being believed or shared.
conclusion: Do you think India should create a separate deepfake law, or are existing legal tools enough to handle this growing threat?
